clue.text: Intellectuals ignoring popular composer

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so one word is dropped from the other here

parts.note: Brahmins are cultured intellectuals, from the highest Hindu caste
in means popular, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Highbrows turn their noses up at a crowd-pleasing composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a nineteenth-century German composer of symphonies and concertos.

clue.text: Loudmouth might be better shutting stupid trap

indicators.note: shutting something in means enclosing it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a better is one who bets, i.e. a backer

indicators.note: stupid means the following word is scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler might tell a noisy person to shut their stupid mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'improved' but means one who places bets. 'stupid' scrambles the letters of trap before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brat Packer was one of the brash young Hollywood stars of the 1980s, noisy celebrities by reputation.

clue.text: Russian cooperative ousting Communist leader from monopoly

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so a letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a cartel is a group controlling a market, a monopoly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Soviet collective throws the party chief out of a commercial monopoly.
explanation.definitionFit: An artel was a cooperative association of workers or craftsmen in Russia.

clue.text: Horse conveying unscrupulous writer

indicators.note: conveying means carrying, so the horse carries another piece inside it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
low means base or unscrupulous

explanation.surface: A horse carries a shady author.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan playwright and poet, author of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: After alcoholic drinks, this writer's game

indicators.note: the writer's word comes after the drinks, placing it at the end

parts.note: gin is one alcoholic drink
rum is another alcoholic drink
the setter speaking of themself: this writer's means my

explanation.surface: After a few drinks, the author's game is on.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a card game for two players, a variety of rummy.

clue.text: Following, one won't get free

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: to get free is to break loose, so the letters escape their order and rearrange

parts.note: the word won't, letters taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn refuses to be released.
explanation.definitionFit: In tow means following along behind, like a vehicle being towed.

clue.text: Company of actors stand up, given encore

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre company
to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: Actors take a standing ovation and give an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated performance of a piece, much like an encore.

clue.text: Fellow keeping you safe at first in farm building

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the fellow surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a fellow is a male
thou is the old form of you

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A man keeps someone safe inside a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A malthouse is a building where grain is malted, often on or near a farm.

clue.text: Rabbi's words of dismay over child's toy

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: oy is a Yiddish cry of dismay, here said twice

explanation.surface: A rabbi groans over a child's plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spinning toy on a string that climbs and falls.

clue.text: Simple man's joke is out of order

indicators.note: is out of means sits outside, so the man's piece wraps around the order

parts.note: man's read as 'he is', contracted to he's
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated fellow's wisecrack is inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' looks like an anagram signal or a rebuke, but 'is out of' is a container signal, and the Order of Merit is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun describes something plain and unsophisticated, like cloth spun at home.

clue.text: Towards end of Jumbo, set format varies

indicators.note: varies means changes, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A jumbo jet's layout changes from one flight to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' looks like part of the wordplay but belongs to the definition: a jumbo jet's tail is aft.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftermost means nearest the stern or tail, the rearmost part of a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: China may be so, having power backed by friendly state?

indicators.note: backed by means supported from behind, so the state follows the power in order

parts.note: an ally is a friendly state

explanation.surface: China, as a world power, may want a friendly neighbouring state.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, and a mate is friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A china, rhyming slang for a mate, is matey and friendly by nature.

clue.text: Join in effort to drag a few stones?

definitions.meaning: to do one's fair share of the work
literally to haul a body weight, measured in stones, the British unit of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to help with a job that means hauling rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do your fair share of a group task.

clue.text: Nurse touches leg and I sit up in pain

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from bottom to top, so it is backwards

explanation.surface: A nurse feels a patient's leg as they sit up hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touches' just joins nurse and leg. In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendonitis is painful inflammation of a tendon.

clue.text: Roughly the price paid for old car

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about or roughly
a rate is a price charged or paid

explanation.surface: Someone pays about the going price for a vintage motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is slang for a battered old car or aeroplane.

clue.text: An awfully violent work of fiction

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the next word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A novel full of gruesome violence.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinovel is a work of fiction that rejects the usual conventions of the novel.

clue.text: Action taken to get journalist admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to procure is to get
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Steps are taken to get a reporter into the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is a course of action taken, a set way of doing something.

clue.text: Cheerful sort, one going after small part in love film

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the love and film pieces

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a film is a thin layer, a mist

indicators.note: going after means following, so one comes after the small part

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for part
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An upbeat actor chases a bit part in a romantic movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimist is a hopeful person who expects the best, a cheerful sort.

clue.text: Anisette concoction Monsieur imbibed … here?

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so one piece is taken inside the other
a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Frenchman drinks an aniseed cocktail somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges ANISETTE into ESTAINET; M goes inside. The whole clue also hints where the drinking happens.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe or bar where a Frenchman might sip anisette.

clue.text: Woman wants beer followed by wine

indicators.note: followed by means the next piece comes after this one

parts.note: mild is a dark, lightly hopped British beer
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A woman wants a pint and then a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a British style of dark, low-strength beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Blue pictures initially discovered in mail

indicators.note: discovered in means found inside, so a letter sits within the other word

parts.note: to mail is to send

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Smutty photos were found in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue pictures' looks like one phrase for porn, but 'Blue' alone is the definition: to blow money.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is old British slang for squandering it, laying it out freely.

clue.text: Artist suffering more over time

indicators.note: in a down clue over means one piece sits above the next

parts.note: sicker means more ill, suffering more

explanation.surface: A painter grows more ill as time goes by.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was a British painter, linked to the Camden Town Group.

clue.text: Book dodgy act in men's club that's apparently empty?

indicators.note: dodgy means suspect or unsound, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: O looks like a zero, an empty ring with nothing in it

explanation.surface: A suspect show is put on in a gentlemen's club that seems deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Tom's Cabin is Harriet Beecher Stowe's 1852 anti-slavery novel.

clue.text: Shakespearian role welcomed by antimonarchist

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by, so the word sits inside the longer one

explanation.surface: A republican is happy to receive a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is the title character of a Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Stand for running water

definitions.meaning: to tolerate or put up with, as in 'I won't stand for it'

explanation.definitionFit: Brook means to tolerate, and a brook is also a small stream.

clue.text: Cannabis is a disappointment

explanation.surface: Someone finds their marijuana a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow is slang for cannabis, and a blow is also a setback or letdown.

clue.text: Heavy bar woman clasped in both hands

indicators.note: clasped in means held inside, so one piece is put between the others

parts.note: L and R, left and right hands
Eve is the first woman of the Bible

explanation.surface: A heavy metal bar is held by a woman in both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid bar used to shift heavy loads.

clue.text: Excludes debs?

definitions.meaning: debutantes are young women, misses, who are coming out into society

explanation.definitionFit: Misses out means omits, and debs are young misses who come out into society.

clue.text: By no means rare expression of approval

definitions.meaning: of a steak, cooked right through
a cry of praise for good work

explanation.surface: Someone praises a steak that is anything but bloody.
explanation.definitionFit: Well done describes thoroughly cooked meat and is also said in praise.

clue.text: Having succeeded, accepts prize money

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
to take is to accept

explanation.surface: A winner accepts the cash prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes is the money competed for in a race or contest.
